supported_static_contracts.registration: Win64 RCX is preserved incoming first argument, RDX is library name, R8 is a temporary null-terminated array of 16-byte name/function pairs; caller returns EAX=1 after registration.
supported_static_contracts.IsSessionConnect: Win64 RCX is preserved as an opaque VM-state argument. It calls the shared accessor, defaults false on null, otherwise tests virtual-slot result with mask 0xFFFFFFF6, pushes one boolean-shaped value and returns EAX=1. The native return is the Lua result count, not the connection boolean.
supported_static_contracts.GetSessionMemberCount: Win64 RCX is preserved as an opaque VM-state argument. It defaults a signed 32-bit count to zero, calls the shared accessor, then calls slot +0x18 on the subobject at +0x20 when nonnull. It sign-extends the count into RDX, pushes one number-shaped value and returns EAX=1. The native return is not the session count.
supported_static_contracts.VM_slot_shapes: The boolean helper writes tag 1 plus normalized boolean; the integer helper converts signed RDX to double and writes tag 3. Both obtain the top slot from RCX+0x10 and advance it by 16 bytes. These observations do not authorize direct structure writes.

critical_limitations: Bindings and ABI shapes are statically associated, not runtime-approved hook targets.
Both named queries call a common accessor with conditional initialization/helper calls; active polling is not established as side-effect-free.
The original registration wrapper changes/restores additional VM flags and records library metadata; calling a bare standard Lua registration function would bypass observed behavior.
The game state argument, stack availability, owning thread, state destruction/replacement and registration timing relative to DirectInput remain unobserved.
The temporary registration table belongs to the registrar's stack and cannot be retained after it returns.
A session count does not prove allocated remote player characters or four-player gameplay.
